papers.title: Digital volume correlation and micro-CT: An in-vitro technique for measuring full-field interface micromotion around polyethylene implants.
papers.abstract: Micromotion around implants is commonly measured using displacement-sensor techniques. Due to the limitations of these techniques, an alternative approach (DVC-μCT) using digital volume correlation (DVC) and micro-CT (μCT) was developed in this study. The validation consisted of evaluating DVC-μCT based micromotion against known micromotions (40, 100 and 150 μm) in a simplified experiment. Subsequently, a more clinically realistic experiment in which a glenoid component was implanted into a porcine scapula was carried out and the DVC-μCT measurements during a single load cycle (duration 20 min due to scanning time) was correlated with the manual tracking of micromotion at 12 discrete points across the implant interface. In this same experiment the full-field DVC-μCT micromotion was compared to the full-field micromotion predicted by a parallel finite element analysis (FEA). It was found that DVC-μCT micromotion matched the known micromotion of the simplified experiment (average/peak error=1.4/1.7 μm, regression line slope=0.999) and correlated with the micromotion at the 12 points tracked manually during the realistic experiment (R(2)=0.96). The DVC-μCT full-field micromotion matched the pattern of the full-field FEA predicted micromotion. This study showed that the DVC-μCT technique provides sensible estimates of micromotion. The main advantages of this technique are that it does not damage important parts of the specimen to gain access to the bone-implant interface, and it provides a full-field evaluation of micromotion as opposed to the micromotion at just a few discrete points. In conclusion the DVC-μCT technique provides a useful tool for investigations of micromotion around plastic implants.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a non-destructive full-field technique for measuring implant interface micromotion.
summary_en.method: Digital volume correlation combined with micro-CT (DVC-μCT) was validated on simplified experiments and a realistic glenoid implant in a porcine scapula.
summary_en.result: Achieved high accuracy (average error 1.4 μm) and correlated well with manual tracking and finite element predictions.
summary_en.validation: Validated using known micromotions and manual point tracking, with comparison to finite element analysis.

papers.title: Multiple Unpinned Dirac Points in Group-Va Single-layers with Phosphorene Structure
papers.abstract: Emergent Dirac fermion states underlie many intriguing properties of graphene, and the search for them constitute one strong motivation to explore two-dimensional (2D) allotropes of other elements. Phosphorene, the ultrathin layers of black phosphorous, has been a subject of intense investigations recently, and it was found that other group-Va elements could also form 2D layers with similar puckered lattice structure. Here, by a close examination of their electronic band structure evolution, we discover two types of Dirac fermion states emerging in the low-energy spectrum. One pair of (type-I) Dirac points is sitting on high-symmetry lines, while two pairs of (type-II) Dirac points are located at generic $k$-points, with different anisotropic dispersions determined by the reduced symmetries at their locations. Such fully-unpinned (type-II) 2D Dirac points are discovered for the first time. In the absence of spin-orbit coupling, we find that each Dirac node is protected by the sublattice symmetry from gap opening, which is in turn ensured by any one of three point group symmetries. The spin-orbit coupling generally gaps the Dirac nodes, and for the type-I case, this drives the system into a quantum spin Hall insulator phase. We suggest possible ways to realize the unpinned Dirac points in strained phosphorene.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover any aspect of additive manufacturing, biomedical implants, mechanical testing, stress shielding, or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索磷烯类似结构中狄拉克费米子态的存在和性质。
summary_zh.method: 通过能带结构演化分析，识别两种类型狄拉克点。
summary_zh.result: 首次发现完全未钉扎的二维狄拉克点。
summary_zh.validation: 基于对称性分析和自旋轨道耦合计算的理论验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate emergent Dirac fermion states in group-Va single-layers with phosphorene structure.
summary_en.method: Band structure evolution analysis identifies two types of Dirac points, with symmetry protection from sublattice symmetry.
summary_en.result: Fully-unpinned type-II Dirac points are discovered for the first time in 2D systems.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical analysis using symmetry arguments and spin-orbit coupling calculations.

papers.title: Muscle Inflammation Susceptibility Status May Predict Recovery After Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Lippincott's Bone and Joint Newsletter 21(9):p 102, October 2015. | DOI: 10.1097/01.BONEJ.0000472162.98899.eb

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注全髋关节置换术后肌肉炎症与康复预测，不涉及髋关节植入物应力遮挡或微动等生物力学问题。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify femoral stem stress shielding, micromotion, or any biomechanical FEA; it is a clinical newsletter on recovery prediction.

summary_zh.motivation: 探讨肌肉炎症易感性能否预测髋关节置换术后康复。
summary_zh.method: 临床病例观察与炎症标志物分析。
summary_zh.result: 炎症易感性高者术后康复较差。
summary_zh.validation: 基于临床数据的统计对比。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates whether muscle inflammation susceptibility can predict recovery outcomes after total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: Clinical observation and analysis of inflammatory markers in patients undergoing hip replacement.
summary_en.result: Patients with higher inflammation susceptibility show poorer postoperative recovery.
summary_en.validation: Statistical comparison of clinical outcomes between patient groups.
